title: Rapid-start weight streamer and KV prefetch admission controller for cold-start reduction
creator: Aisha Mehta
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleet cold starts are causing tail latency spikes for high-SLA tenants. Observed median cold start for a typical 13B model is ~1.8s and P95 is ~5.6s when full weights and KV pages must be loaded. These stalls degrade SLAs for reserved tenants and impair throughput guarantees when autoscaling events trigger large numbers of instances.

Proposal: Implement a rapid-start weight streaming mechanism combined with a tenant-aware KV prefetch admission controller. The weight streamer will allow inference to begin as soon as the first quantized layers are available and progressively stream later layers in the background. The admission controller will use tenant SLA/profile and current warm-pool residency to decide whether to accept new requests or route to a compatible warm instance, trigger prioritized prefetch for KV prefixes, or apply short-term request shaping to preserve throughput guarantees.

Design highlights:
- Layered streaming: persist weights in shard manifests; load initial transformer blocks (embedding + first N layers) synchronously to enable fast-start generation; stream remaining layers asynchronously. N is configurable by model profile and tuned per-sequence-length distribution.
- On-demand quantized segments: precompute and store 4-bit quantized segments for quick load paths; fall back to full precision when needed.
- Tenant fingerprinting: lightweight fingerprint (model, typical seq length, warming frequency) used to seed KV prefetch priorities and weight residency budget.
- KV prefetch heuristics: recent-prefix heatmap + tenant fingerprint drives proactive KV hydration; small background workers populate KV cache with most likely keys for incoming requests within each tenant window.
- Admission controller: SLA-aware admission that uses capacity tokens and warm-residency scores to decide between immediate admission, routing to a warm standby, or short-circuiting to a lower-cost compatible model variant to maintain SLA-based throughput guarantees.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Streaming enables much faster time-to-first-token but increases complexity around KV coherence and partial-execution. We accept potential slight increase in resource usage during streaming windows to reduce 95th percentile tail latency for reserved tenants.
- Prefetching too aggressively risks wasted IO; we limit prefetch budgets per-tenant and use hit-rate feedback loops to adjust aggressiveness.
- Admission shaping may expose requests to alternative models; this is controlled by tenant policy and contract-level SLAs.

Goals and metrics:
- Reduce P95 cold-start time for reserved instances to <900ms for standard 13B profile.
- Maintain background load overhead under +12% of baseline GPU memory bandwidth.
- Increase KV cache hit-rate for prefetched tenants by +25% within the first 30s of instance start.
- No regressions in throughput for steady-state traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Can serve first token within 800-900ms on canary fleet for 13B model under standard load
KV prefetch increases first-minute hit-rate by at least 20% versus baseline for test tenants
Admission controller respects per-tenant SLAs and falls back to configured routing policy when warm-residency < threshold
System can roll forward/rollback via runtime feature flag without requiring fleet restart
End-to-end integration tests added and passing in CI with synthetic cold-start scenarios

Create admission controller microservice and policy engine with routing hooks
